units.source_text: 且说柏木卫门督闻知了公主生育和出家等事，病势更加沉重起来，全然少有希望了。

en.t: Now Kashiwagi, the Captain of the Gate Guards, heard of the princess's childbirth and tonsure, and his illness grew still more grave, leaving almost no hope.

units.source_text: 他可怜他的妻子落叶公主，想道：“叫她到这里来，似乎太轻率了。

en.t: He pitied his wife, Princess Ochiba, and thought, "To call her here would seem far too rash.

units.source_text: 况且母夫人和父大臣都常常来我身边，一不小心，二公主的御容自然会被他们看到，这就尴尬了。”

en.t: Besides, my mother and my father the minister often come to my side; if I am careless, they will naturally see the Second Princess's face, and that would be awkward."

units.source_text: 他就向父母亲请求：“我有点事，想到公主那里去一趟。”

en.t: So he asked his parents, "There is something I must attend to, and I would like to go once to the princess's residence."

units.source_text: 但父母亲断然不许。

en.t: But his parents flatly refused to allow it.

units.source_text: 于是他看见无论何人，都诉说想见落叶公主的话。

en.t: After that, whenever he saw anyone at all, he spoke of his longing to see Princess Ochiba.

units.source_text: 落叶公主的母夫人最初原不赞成把女儿嫁给柏木。

en.t: Princess Ochiba's mother had originally been opposed to marrying her daughter to Kashiwagi.

units.source_text: 只因柏木的父亲亲自奔走，再三恳求，朱雀院被他的诚意所感动，无可奈何，便把女儿许给了他。

en.t: But Kashiwagi's father had personally exerted himself and pleaded again and again, and Suzaku-in, moved by his sincerity and seeing no alternative, had granted him his daughter.

units.source_text: 朱雀院为三公主和源氏的婚事担心的时候曾经说：“二公主倒反而有了一个可靠的丈夫，不须担心将来的事呢。”

en.t: When Suzaku-in was worried about the marriage of the Third Princess and Genji, he had once said, "The Second Princess, by contrast, has found a dependable husband, so there is no need to worry about her future."

units.source_text: 柏木传闻到这句话，深为感激。

en.t: When Kashiwagi heard of these words, he was deeply grateful.

units.source_text: 此时对母亲说道：“我想，我倘抛开她而死去，她真要受苦了。

en.t: Now he said to his mother, "I think that if I die and leave her behind, she will truly suffer.

units.source_text: 但天命如此，无可奈何，因缘不长，此恨绵绵！

en.t: But if this is Heaven's decree, there is nothing to be done; our bond was not to last, and this sorrow will never end.

units.source_text: 她的悲伤愁叹实在是很可怜的。

en.t: Her grief and lamentation are truly pitiful.

units.source_text: 为此请求父母亲格外垂青，多多照拂。”

en.t: For that reason, I ask you and Father to show her special kindness and look after her well."

units.source_text: 母亲答道：“哎呀，你莫说这不祥的话！

en.t: His mother answered, "Oh, do not say such unlucky things!

units.source_text: 你倘先死了，我们还有几多余命，可以接受你这来日方长的嘱咐呢？”

en.t: If you were to die before us, how much life would we have left to take on such a long future charge from you?"

units.source_text: 说着只是哭泣。

en.t: As she said this, she could only weep.

units.source_text: 柏木不便再求，只得找他的弟弟左大弁商量，详细委托他种种事情。

en.t: Kashiwagi could not press his request any further, so he had no choice but to consult his younger brother, the Left Senior Controller, and entrust all sorts of matters to him in detail.

units.source_text: 柏木秉性温良，和蔼可亲，所以他的诸弟，尤其是年幼的诸弟，都信赖他，视同父母一样。

en.t: Kashiwagi was gentle by nature and easy to love, so all his younger brothers, especially the youngest ones, trusted him and regarded him almost as a parent.

units.source_text: 现在听他说这些痛心的话，没有一个人不悲伤，邸内的人也都愁叹。

en.t: Now, hearing him say such heartbreaking things, there was not one of them who did not grieve, and everyone in the household lamented as well.

units.source_text: 皇上闻知他病重，也深为惋惜。

en.t: When the emperor heard that his illness was serious, he too felt deep regret.

units.source_text: 听说病已无望，立刻下诏，晋封他为权大纳言。

en.t: On hearing that there was no longer any hope for his recovery, he immediately issued an edict promoting him to Acting Major Counselor.

units.source_text: 又对左右说道：“他闻此喜讯，或能起床，再度入宫，亦未可知。”

en.t: He also said to those around him, "If he hears this joyful news, he may be able to rise from his bed and come to court once more."

units.source_text: 然而柏木病势并无好转，只能忍着痛苦，伏枕谢恩而已。

en.t: But Kashiwagi's condition did not improve at all, and he could only endure his suffering and give thanks from his pillow.

units.source_text: 父大臣看见圣眷如此优厚，越发悲恸不堪，但也惟有徒唤奈何耳。

en.t: Seeing the emperor's favor toward him so generous, his father the minister was all the more overcome with grief, yet there was nothing he could do but lament helplessly.
